From 581073f626e387d3e7eed55c48c8495584ead7ba Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2024 16:33:58 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] af_packet: do not call packet_read_pending() from
 tpacket_destruct_skb()

trafgen performance considerably sank on hosts with many cores
after the blamed commit.

packet_read_pending() is very expensive, and calling it
in af_packet fast path defeats Daniel intent in commit
b013840810c2 ("packet: use percpu mmap tx frame pending refcount")

tpacket_destruct_skb() makes room for one packet, we can immediately
wakeup a producer, no need to completely drain the tx ring.

Fixes: 89ed5b519004 ("af_packet: Block execution of tasks waiting for transmit to complete in AF_PACKET")
Signed-off-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Cc: Neil Horman <nhorman@tuxdriver.com>
Cc: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
Reviewed-by: Willem de Bruijn <willemb@google.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240515163358.4105915-1-edumazet@google.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/packet/af_packet.c b/net/packet/af_packet.c
index 8c6d3fbb4ed8..ea3ebc160e25 100644
--- a/net/packet/af_packet.c
+++ b/net/packet/af_packet.c
@@ -2522,8 +2522,7 @@ static void tpacket_destruct_skb(struct sk_buff *skb)
 		ts = __packet_set_timestamp(po, ph, skb);
 		__packet_set_status(po, ph, TP_STATUS_AVAILABLE | ts);
 
-		if (!packet_read_pending(&po->tx_ring))
-			complete(&po->skb_completion);
+		complete(&po->skb_completion);
 	}
 
 	sock_wfree(skb);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `net/packet/af_packet.c`**
- The function `tpacket_destruct_skb()` was modified to remove the call to `packet_read_pending(&po->tx_ring)`.
- The line that checks for pending packets and conditionally calls `complete(&po->skb_completion)` was replaced with a direct call to `complete(&po->skb_completion)` without the condition.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modification in `tpacket_destruct_skb()` aims to improve performance by eliminating the expensive call to `packet_read_pending()` in the fast path of the AF_PACKET processing. This change is intended to enhance the performance of trafgen on multi-core hosts, as the previous implementation was causing a significant performance drop. By directly completing the skb completion without checking for pending packets, the function can now more efficiently signal that a packet has been processed, aligning with the intent of previous commits to optimize transmit frame handling.

Here is the commit message:
af_packet: do not call packet_read_pending() from
 tpacket_destruct_skb()

trafgen performance considerably sank on hosts with many cores
after the blamed commit.

packet_read_pending() is very expensive, and calling it
in af_packet fast path defeats Daniel intent in commit
b013840810c2 ("packet: use percpu mmap tx frame pending refcount")

tpacket_destruct_skb() makes room for one packet, we can immediately
wakeup a producer, no need to completely drain the tx ring.

Fixes: 89ed5b519004 ("af_packet: Block execution of tasks waiting for transmit to complete in AF_PACKET")
Signed-off-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Cc: Neil Horman <nhorman@tuxdriver.com>
Cc: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
Reviewed-by: Willem de Bruijn <willemb@google.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240515163358.4105915-1-edumazet@google.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The root cause of the bug is the expensive call to `packet_read_pending()` within the `tpacket_destruct_skb()` function, which is part of the AF_PACKET fast path. This call negatively impacts performance, especially on hosts with many cores, as it introduces unnecessary overhead in a critical path where packets are being processed. The intent of the previous commit was to optimize the handling of transmit frames, but the inclusion of this call counteracted those optimizations, leading to degraded performance in trafgen.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void tpacket_destruct_skb(struct sk_buff *skb)
 {
 	struct packet_sock *po = pkt_sk(skb->sk);
 
 	if (likely(po->tx_ring.pg_vec)) {
 		void *ph;
 		__u32 ts;
 
 		ph = skb_zcopy_get_nouarg(skb);
 		packet_dec_pending(&po->tx_ring);
 
 		ts = __packet_set_timestamp(po, ph, skb);
 		__packet_set_status(po, ph, TP_STATUS_AVAILABLE | ts);
 
-		if (!packet_read_pending(&po->tx_ring))
-			complete(&po->skb_completion);
+		complete(&po->skb_completion);
 	}
 
 	sock_wfree(skb);
 }
